items.claim: The superscription spans exactly Jer.1.1-1.3, closing before the first word-event formula, and its cited marks and Hebrew are byte-accurate.
items.evidence: The title formula דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֑הוּ מִן הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֔וֹת בְּאֶ֖רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן (oshb:Jer.1.1, byte tier) collates byte-exact, and the three-reign date span through Jer.1.3 (Josiah, then Jehoiakim and Zedekiah's eleventh year) matches the source. The setumah cited at Jer.1.3 is confirmed present in the parashah inventory as SAMEKH, not conflated with petuchah, and is correctly disclosed as single-witness tier-3 corroboration rather than the boundary's driver; the actual driver, the vayehi-devar-YHWH formula at Jer.1.4, is one of the book's three fixed word-event shapes and sits correctly outside this span. No universal or exclusivity wording appears, and superscription is the correct unit_type for a title-and-provenance heading carrying no narrative or oracle content of its own.

items.claim: The call-narrative dialogue at Jer.1.4-1.10 is bounded on both ends by verse-initial word-event formulas, and its internal petuchah citations match the inventory exactly.
items.evidence: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.1.4, byte tier) collates byte-exact as the opening word-event formula, and the adonai-YHWH title stack quoted from Jer.1.6, וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה לֹא יָדַ֖עְתִּי דַּבֵּ֑ר כִּי נַ֖עַר אָנֹֽכִי, also collates byte-exact. The fresh word-event formula that closes this unit opens at Jer.1.11, outside the span. Both petuchah citations, after Jer.1.6 and after Jer.1.10, are confirmed PE at those exact verses in the parashah inventory, and the setumah disclosed immediately before the span's own opening, at Jer.1.3, is likewise confirmed. The rescue-clause recurrence between Jer.1.8 and Jer.1.19 is disclosed with the hedged phrase 'recurs in close wording' rather than a stronger identity claim, which matches the actual byte-level relationship between the two clauses (see the Jer.1.17-1.19 item for the collation).

items.claim: The two-verse vision report at Jer.1.11-1.12 is bounded by its own word-event formula and closes exactly where the next one begins, with matching petuchah marks on both sides.
items.evidence: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר מָה אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וָאֹמַ֕ר מַקֵּ֥ל שָׁקֵ֖ד אֲנִ֥י רֹאֶֽה (oshb:Jer.1.11, byte tier) and וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י הֵיטַ֣בְתָּ לִרְא֑וֹת כִּֽי שֹׁקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י עַל דְּבָרִ֖י לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.1.12, byte tier) both collate byte-exact, including the 'what do you see' vision-question formula and the shoqed reply. The next word-event formula, explicitly marked 'a second time,' opens fresh at Jer.1.13, immediately outside the span. The petuchah citations after Jer.1.10 and after Jer.1.12 both match the parashah inventory exactly. The shaqed/shoqed pun is correctly named by its own root and explicitly distinguished from the unrelated sheqer keyword, avoiding the two-letter-overlap sweep hazard that root carries elsewhere in the book.

items.claim: The second vision report and its interpretation, Jer.1.13-1.16, hold together as one unit under one word-event formula, since no tier-1 marker intervenes, closing where a discourse imperative opens the next unit.
items.evidence: The 'second time' word-event formula, וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר סִ֤יר נָפ֨וּחַ֙ אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֔ה וּפָנָ֖יו מִפְּנֵ֥י צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier), collates byte-exact; Jer.1.14-1.16 add neither a fresh formula, an imperative, nor an addressee shift, so keeping the vision and its interpretation in one span is consistent with the book's word-event skeleton. The next unit's imperative onset, at Jer.1.17, is a valid discourse-imperative seam. The petuchah citation standing at Jer.1.12, immediately before the span opens, corresponds to the inventory; the parashah inventory also confirms the claimed silence across Jer.1.13-1.18, holding its next petuchah back until Jer.1.19.

items.claim: The imperative-marked charge at Jer.1.17-1.19 is a sound seam, but its inclusio claim overstates the byte relationship between the two rescue clauses it brackets.
items.evidence: The rescue clause quoted from Jer.1.19, וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹא י֣וּכְלוּ לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier), is called 'the same rescue clause that closed' Jer.1.8, אַל תִּירָ֖א מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier) -- but collation shows the two clauses invert the order of 'declares Yahweh' against the infinitive 'to rescue you,' and spell that infinitive differently (defective letters lamed-he-tsadi-tsadi-lamed-kaf at Jer.1.8 versus plene lamed-he-tsadi-tsadi-yod-lamed-kaf at Jer.1.19, an inserted yod). The shared elements support a recurring formula, not byte identity, so 'the same...clause' overclaims what the source shows; a hedge such as 'closely worded recurrence' would match the bytes. This does not disturb the seam itself: the imperative construction opening Jer.1.17 and the addressee shift back to Jeremiah are independently valid grounds, and the petuchah closing the span at Jer.1.19 matches the inventory. The boundary_evidence_refs entry for Jer.1.4, raised elsewhere as an orphan citation, is grounded in the same sentence's reference to 'the call narrative' that Jer.1.4 opens, and is a heuristic artifact rather than a fabricated or mis-resolved reference.

items.claim: The covenant-memory oracle at Jer.2.1-2.3 opens on a fresh word-event formula and closes on a matching petuchah exactly where the next imperative-marked unit begins.
items.evidence: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.2.1, byte tier) collates byte-exact as the word-event formula opening chapter 2, and the go-and-proclaim clause with its koh-amar oracle opening, הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ לֶכְתֵּ֤ךְ אַחֲרַי֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א זְרוּעָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), also collates byte-exact against the source. The petuchah citations bracketing the span, at Jer.1.19 before it and Jer.2.3 at its own close, both match the inventory, and the next attend-the-word imperative opens cleanly at Jer.2.4 with no intervening mark or formula. The judgment_oracle label is defended against the real salvation_oracle rival on content grounds -- the unit's own close threatens those who wrong Israel rather than promising Israel's restoration -- which is the strongest available choice given the closed unit_type vocabulary.

items.claim: The trial-speech boundaries at Jer.2.4-2.13 are sound, but one internal rib-pattern element is mislabeled: the contention formula at Jer.2.9 is called a verdict, when it is the lawsuit's own opening declaration rather than a ruling.
items.evidence: Jer.2.9, לָכֵ֗ן עֹ֛ד אָרִ֥יב אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אָרִֽיב (oshb:Jer.2.9, byte tier) -- YHWH's own announcement of future contention against the audience -- uses the root that names the covenant-lawsuit genre itself (the same root recurs reflexively at Jer.2.29, where YHWH turns the dispute-verb back on the audience), announcing that litigation is beginning rather than closing it; no sentence or ruling is pronounced anywhere in Jer.2.4-2.13, since what follows is evidentiary -- the heavens-and-coastlands witness summons at Jer.2.10 and Jer.2.12 -- and the span closes on the twin-evil indictment at Jer.2.13, itself a charge rather than a verdict. The entry seam is solid regardless: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) collates byte-exact as the attend-the-word imperative, and the petuchah standing at Jer.2.3 immediately before the span matches the inventory.

items.claim: The entry seam at Jer.2.14 rests on a shift to a sustained run of rhetorical questions, a rhetorical-mode and topic observation rather than one of the book's tier-1 seam classes, so the case for a fresh unit beginning there is no stronger than the internal metaphor-shift cuts this unit's own rationale rejects.
items.evidence: No word-event formula, koh-amar onset carrying a frame-owner change, discourse imperative, date onset, or vision opening falls between the attend-the-word imperative at Jer.2.4 and the next attend-the-word imperative at Jer.2.31; the koh-amar that opens Jer.2.5 re-marks the same YHWH frame already open since Jer.2.1 rather than changing it, so it does not qualify under the frame-owner-change rule either. On the book's own word-event and imperative skeleton, the entire Jer.2.4-2.30 stretch is therefore one unmarked run, and the split at the Jer.2.13/2.14 seam rests on a shift in rhetorical register -- הַעֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָבַֽז (oshb:Jer.2.14, byte tier) opens a run of interrogatives about Israel's status and history, after the formal summons-and-witness language of Jer.2.4-2.13 -- rather than on a formula, addressee change, or scene marker. The unit's own trailing edge compounds the gap: a neum-YHWH closure falls at Jer.2.29, לָ֥מָּה תָרִ֖יבוּ אֵלָ֑י כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier), one verse before the claimed close at Jer.2.30, and strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only the internal metaphor-shift candidates at Jer.2.21, Jer.2.23, and Jer.2.27, never the closer, formula-adjacent rival of ending at Jer.2.29 instead. The parashah layer is silent across the whole span except the setumah at Jer.2.28, correctly disclosed as non-driving texture, so no tier-3 corroboration resolves the question either way.
